explanation: Perform an iterative inorder traversal and count visited nodes. Return the Data of the kth visited node. This follows the displayed contract without relying on precomputed subtree sizes.
timeComplexity: O(h + k) time for height h, at most O(n). Counting traversal visits k nodes plus an initial path; size-guided native searches take one path without visiting skipped subtrees.
spaceComplexity: O(h) auxiliary space. C#/JavaScript retain an inorder stack; native size-guided code keeps a cursor and local rank.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: The explicit stack simulates recursive inorder: it delays each root until its left subtree has been exhausted, then continues right. Thus the visitation counter decrements in exact inorder order, and the visit that changes k to zero contains the requested node’s Data.
walkthrough: For [8,4,12,2,6,10,14], inorder is [2,4,6,8,10,12,14]. Counting five visited nodes reaches 10, so return 10. JSON arguments are [tree,k]. Native wrappers populate subtree sizes and observe the returned node’s data; C#/JavaScript count inorder visits directly.
edgeCases: The requested value is inorder rank, not breadth-first array position.
This implementation does not depend on populated Size fields.
